prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near vehicle interior—roof, windshield edges, mirror, dashboard, and occasional hand, roughly 0.2–1.5 m away—from the road, houses, trees, and parked vehicles several metres to tens of metres ahead. Across the five frames, the viewpoint rotates between left-oblique and forward road views; fixed cabin surfaces remain close while the outdoor layout shifts laterally, with no clear evidence of approach or retreat over this short sequence. No other person is spatially resolved, and nothing outside the vehicle is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach; parts of the cabin occlude the upper and lower scene and some surfaces extend out of frame. The map makes broad near/far layers clearer than RGB, but its bright sky and distant background, dark treatment of some nearby cabin surfaces, missing fine structures, and inconsistent boundaries make metric distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map mainly identifies vehicles: the camera wearer’s own surrounding vehicle interior is represented by a very large, partly out-of-view car mask in the second frame, while several small car masks lie along or beside the road roughly 10–40 m away in later frames. A small person-labelled region near the lower edge of the second frame corresponds to a nearby, partly occluded body/hand area within about 0.3–1 m, whereas no outside pedestrian is reliably segmented or shown facing the camera. The masks reveal separate vehicle instances that are easy to overlook in RGB and show their left/right distribution as the view turns, but they provide no direct depth, facing direction, or reliable arm-reach information. Large portions of the visible car interior, road, houses, and vegetation are unlabelled, some distant car masks are tiny or fragmented, and the oversized car mask appears to merge or misclassify cabin regions, so object extent and inter-object spacing are uncertain.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty in all five frames, so it supplies no body or hand joints from which to infer posture, facing direction, gaze, reach, or distances between people. In the RGB strip, only small portions of the camera wearer’s nearby hand/arm appear around the steering area, approximately 0.3–0.7 m from the camera, and no clearly visible external person can be tracked across frames. The black output therefore adds no spatial structure beyond indicating that the pose estimator produced no detections, likely because the visible body parts are small, cropped, or occluded by the vehicle interior. It cannot establish whether anyone turns, approaches, retreats, looks toward the wearer, or has an object within reach.
